the development of novel magnetic materials based on the cyanide ligand, which are characterized by a large variety of magnetic ground states, such as ferromagnetism, ferrimagnetism, spin-glasses and cluster glasses.

the photoinduced magnetization of a Fe–Co cyanine film is the first example of a photoinduced magnetically ordered system.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that photoexcitation of a cluster glass can lead to a substantial increase of magnetization, a change of critical temperatures, a change of the freezing temperature, and an increase of the relaxation time.
the photoinduced magnetic properties of the Fe–Co cyanides are determined by the photoinduced change of the magnetic anisotropy.
photoexcitation of the cyanide ligand field states in the Fe–Co cyanides leads to a change of the magnetic ground state.

the magnetic behavior of this system can be controlled by light.
the photoexcitation of a cluster-glass system leads to a significant change in the magnetic properties, which can be used to tune the magnetism of a material.
